item.title: Road Work: Ariana Grande’s First Tour in Seven Years Squeezes Multiple Eras Into One Show
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to Pop Pulse, your go-to podcast for the latest updates on the music scene. Today, we're talking about one of the most prolific pop stars of the last 15 years - Ariana Grande. She's gearing up to release her eighth studio album since 2013, and her current tour is making waves.
[Soft music transitions in]
Host: The Eternal Sunshine Tour, which marks Grande's first tour in seven years, has already grossed $36 million and sold 203,000 tickets in its first 14 shows, according to Billboard Boxscore. Not bad for a relatively limited tour that'll span less than three months.
[Music transitions to a slightly upbeat tone]
Host: Grande's touring history is interesting. In the early days of her career, she would tour behind each album release. But over time, her output - both recorded and live - has become more unpredictable. After releasing Sweetener in 2018, she announced the Sweetener World Tour, only to release another album, Thank U, Next, just a few months later.
[Music transitions back to a neutral tone]
Host: Fast forward to today, and Grande is in a similar position. The Eternal Sunshine Tour is her first live trek since the release of multiple albums, and she's already teasing new music. In fact, she released a single called "Hate That I Made You Love Me" just before the tour kicked off, which will be part of her upcoming album Petal, dropping on July 29.
[Outro music plays]
Host: As Ariana Grande takes the stage at Brooklyn's Barclays Center for a five-show run, it'll be exciting to see how The Eternal Sunshine Tour compares to her previous runs. We'll be keeping an eye on it. Thanks for tuning in to this episode of Pop Pulse. Stay tuned for more music updates! [Outro music continues to play]
